sections.html:
Romeoville sellers choose between a regular listing, a sale without an agent, and a direct sale to a buyer paying cash. The cash route shortens the timeline most. No matter which you pick, the village's clearance letter and transfer stamp apply to every sale, and the clearance letter expires after five business days, so time your request carefully.

  • A listing exposes the house to the most buyers and usually has the slowest closing.
  • A private sale avoids commission and leaves marketing and negotiation to you.
  • A direct sale to a cash buyer is typically as-is, with a closing date the seller sets.

Romeoville is a Will County village about 26 miles southwest of Chicago, between Bolingbrook and Joliet near Interstates 55 and 355. It has an estimated 41,281 residents, up 1.2% from 2020, and 13,296 households averaging 3.05 people. Ownership dominates: 80.7% of units are owner-occupied. The middle home value is $257,100, the middle gross rent is $1,886, and middle owner cost with a mortgage is $1,934 a month.

Much of the housing went up after the Weber Road interchange opened on I-55 in 1990, so many houses are younger than those in older inner suburbs. Buyers therefore tend to compare condition and finishes. Warehouse, refinery and retail jobs cluster near I-55, and a house with quick access to that interchange gives a buyer a shorter drive to work.

sections.h2: What must happen at the village before closing?
sections.html:
Romeoville's Real Estate Transfer Tax is the buyer's responsibility, but the seller has to clear the property first. To get a transfer stamp, the property must be free of debts to the village, including the most current water bill. You request a clearance letter, which starts the process and orders a final water reading. Letters are valid for five business days. An exempt transaction does not need a final meter reading if the water account is in good standing and the name stays the same.

Romeoville transfer tax
Transaction typeVillage charge
Nonexempt$3.50 per $1,000 of full consideration
Exempt$40 processing fee

You can pay online by credit card or e-check, or in person. After payment you receive a receipt with space for the stamp, and the physical stamp can be handed over or mailed. A lost stamp must be repurchased at full price.

A refund exists only for residents who sell the home they live in and buy another Romeoville home as a new principal residence, with the two deals within 12 months of each other. The Finance Department is at 1050 W Romeo Road, phone 815-886-7212.

The final water bill is part of the clearance. The village mails it to the forwarding address you give after closing. Your account stays in your name until a final on-site meter read is done, so give the Water Billing office your closing date and mailing address ahead of time.

Any unpaid balance blocks the stamp, and that in turn blocks recording. Paying the account in full the day the reading posts keeps the closing on schedule.

sections.h2: State and county stamps on the deed
sections.html:
State law sets the Illinois stamp at 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction, sold through the county recorder (35 ILCS 200/31-15). A deed will not be accepted for filing until those stamps have been bought from the recorder of the county where it is filed (35 ILCS 200/31-20). Romeoville is in Will County, so the recording office there handles the filing. The county sets its own stamp amount and fee schedule, so ask the Will County Clerk's recording office for current figures.

Your title company normally prepares the state transfer declaration and delivers the deed with the village stamp attached.

sections.h2: How Will County property tax works for a seller
sections.html:
Will County mails bills on May 1 for the previous tax year. The first installment comes due in June and the second in September, and postmarks count. Late payments accrue interest under state statute, starting at 1.5% per month on the first installment from June 2, with the rate stepping up in later months.

As a seller, confirm that both installments are paid and settle the proration on the closing statement. The calendar changes yearly, so ask the Will County Treasurer for the schedule that fits your sale date.

A sale here moves faster when you tackle the village steps in order. Plan on this sequence:

  • Once you have a signed contract, request the clearance letter close to the closing date, since it lasts only five business days.
  • Give Water Billing your closing date and forwarding address so the final read is booked.
  • Pay any outstanding village balance, including the water bill, so the stamp can be issued.
  • Ask your title company to prepare the state transfer declaration and collect the county stamp.
  • Confirm the buyer has paid the village transfer tax and that you receive the stamped receipt.
  • Check with the Will County Treasurer that both installments are settled.

A cash buyer does not have a lender's appraisal and underwriting to wait for, so these village steps are often the longest items left on the calendar. Starting them early is the simplest way to keep a quick closing quick.

Some transfers qualify as exempt from the village tax, and those carry the flat $40 processing fee instead of the per-$1,000 charge. The account still has to be in good standing, and the village still wants the clearance letter first. If the same name stays on the water account, no final meter reading is needed. If you think your transfer might be exempt, say so when you call the Finance Department so the right paperwork is prepared from the start. Ask the title company to confirm the exemption before anyone pays the wrong amount.

A cash buyer typically takes the house as is, so you do not repaint, replace flooring or stage rooms. There is no lender appraisal, and the closing date is the one you set. The village paperwork does not disappear, though. The clearance letter, the water read, the stamp and the recorded deed all apply, so a cash sale saves you the lender's timeline and the repair negotiations, not the local steps.

If the house sits empty while you wait, keep the water account current and the property tidy. An open village balance is the most common thing that holds up a stamp.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax in Romeoville?
faqs.a: The buyer is responsible for the village's Real Estate Transfer Tax. The seller still has to clear all village debts first, including the water bill.

faqs.q: How long is a Romeoville clearance letter good for?
faqs.a: Five business days. The letter starts the clearance process and orders the final water reading, so request it close to your closing date.

faqs.q: Do I need a final water reading when I sell in Romeoville?
faqs.a: Usually yes. An exempt transaction can skip it if the account is in good standing and the name stays the same. Otherwise your account stays open until a final on-site read, and the last bill goes to your forwarding address.

faqs.q: Can I get a transfer tax refund in Romeoville?
faqs.a: Only if you live in the home, sell it, and buy another Romeoville home as your new principal residence within 12 months. Owner-occupants who sell and buy outside the village do not qualify.

faqs.q: Which county records a Romeoville deed?
faqs.a: Will County. The deed goes to the Will County recording office with the state and county stamps and the village stamp. Your title company usually files it.
